DECISIVE: during stall, a 1KB pinned DtoH of the RING SLOTS buffer hangs entirely, while 4-byte TAIL control reads succeed — the wave is wedged INSIDE slots-region processing. Mechanism hypothesis (high confidence): ring.enqueue advances device-visible head bookkeeping before its ASYNC descriptor-payload upload lands; an already-hot resident worker claims the slot in that window and executes a half-visible descriptor (garbage bounds/ptrs -> infinite/fault-retry). Idle-launched workers (batch mode, phase0) never hit the window. FIX PATTERN: defer head publication until payload upload confirmed (control-stream barrier after final upload), and/or land payloads synchronously pre-publish

Root cause: unthrottled busy-poll spin (bare continue re-issuing global atomics every cycle from a single 128-thread workgroup) starved/wedged the wave on RDNA4+ROCm7.2 after idle gaps — NOT JIT/module flake, NOT head-payload race (both disproven: publish_head no-op; prov logging showed single FRESH-COMPILE reused across tasks). Fix: bounded exponential __builtin_amdgcn_s_sleep backoff in empty-queue branch (shift 0->6, reset on claim; s_sleep requires constant arg so expressed as repeat loop). VERIFIED on fresh boot, clean system: phase0=2, batch A=4, batch B=6, output parity 2.384e-7, clean shutdown, 0.79s. Regressions: 3/3 ring suite + opcode-6 device gate green. ALSO: (1) blocking hipMemcpy in enqueue deadlocks against eternal kernel (device-scope staging) — uploads are async+control-stream-sync; (2) pageable-staged DtoH (to_cpu_vec_f32) hangs against eternal kernel — readback must follow shutdown() or use control stream; (3) per-call RocmPinnedBuffer::alloc also deadlocks — reuse preallocated cells
